A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GDPO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original opinion-generation and movie-review experiments, training analyses, HH-RLHF belief mining, and evaluator-validation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Table 2, Figures 2–5, and the appendix analyses. Retained results qualify even though the new KTO extension has no experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix J adds a concrete KTO variant of GDPO, replacing the preference-alignment term with a KTO loss whose reward is conditioned on the desirable belief. This is a limited extension of the existing two-part framework; the DPO-based experimental method is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use GlobalOpinionQA-derived opinion generation for the United States, Pakistan, and South Africa, Amazon movie-review generation, and the supplementary HH-RLHF belief-mining sample. No dataset, population, or evaluated task is added.

E2.justification: Opinion-generation comparisons retain few-shot prompting, ICF, SFT, and DPO, with Uniform SFT retained in the training-curve comparison. Movie-review comparisons still use SFT and DPO. KTO is formulated in v2 but is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, model sizes, prompting configurations, metrics, and training settings are unchanged. The experiment-setup text moves verbatim from v1 Section 5.1 to v2 Appendix G; Appendix H also retains the same evaluator-validation procedure.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the loss-term ablations in Figure 4, majority/minority analyses in Figures 2–3, output case study in Table 3, HH-RLHF belief mining, and evaluator validation. The KTO appendix supplies a formulation, not a new ablation or empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the experimental comparisons. The reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 values and the results in Figures 2–5 are unchanged. For example, US GDPO JSD remains 0.188 for GPT-2 Large and 0.068 for Pythia-2.8B. Output examples, training-time measurements, and appendix evaluator-validation outcomes are also retained.

T1.justification: Equation 7 corrects the preference loss from log sigmoid to negative log sigmoid, making it consistent with the stated DPO minimization objective. Appendix J adds the KTO loss definitions and a belief-conditioned adaptation in Equations 8–12. No new theorem or proof is provided.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about distributional alignment, minority preferences, and GDPO's empirical advantages. The KTO appendix concretizes the existing assertion that the framework can accommodate other preference losses.

C2.justification: Interpretations of DPO's minority-preference failures and GDPO's calibration benefits remain unchanged, as do the single-group and explicit-belief limitations. Appendix I's added sentence about latent beliefs repeats a future direction already stated in v1 Section 6.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code/data release, whereas v2's abstract reports that they are released at the same repository. This is a change in reported availability; external availability is not established by the PDFs. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, and timing details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al. (2024b) on personalized language modeling, Siththaranjan et al. (2023) on distributional preference learning, and Ethayarajh et al. (2024) on KTO. These modestly expand the discussion while preserving the reward-free, within-group research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged. v2 moves experimental settings into Appendix G, reorders existing appendices, adds acknowledgments, updates author/header information, and makes localized terminology and related-work edits.

P2.justification: All five figures and nine tables are retained, with relocations, renumbering, and limited table reflow. Figure 3 and Table 2 move earlier, and the HH-RLHF tables move toward the end of the appendix. Charts, axes, legends, and table contents are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation 7 removes an inconsistency in the stated optimization objective, and Appendix J makes the previously asserted flexibility concrete through a KTO formulation. Additional related work and the reported code/data release also improve documentation. These are limited gains: the KTO extension remains unevaluated, and the empirical evidence and substantive limitations are unchanged.
